# Code that was not written for lazy arrays {#sec-ordinary}

```{r}
#| include: false
source("R/book.R")
```

The examples so far could all be rescued today by calling
`altarr_extract()` in place of `[`. This chapter is about why that is
not an answer.

The promise of a classless ALTREP array is that it *is* an array. Nobody
has to write methods for it and nobody has to know it is lazy. Thirty
years of R code takes arrays and indexes them with `[`. Every one of
those functions works on a lazy array on stock R, correctly, and reads
its data one element at a time. A special extract function helps only the
code that calls it.

With the method in R, the planning happens underneath `[`, so it happens
for all of them.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| file: scripts/07-ordinary.R
```

```{r}
res <- book_run("07-ordinary.R")
book_table(res)
```

Read by read:

- **Negative, logical and character subscripts.** R resolves all of them
  to positions before the method is called, with its own rules for
  recycling, name matching and `NA`. A lazy array class gets R's full
  indexing language without implementing any of it, and cannot get it
  subtly wrong.
- **`apply()` over a block.** The function takes an array and indexes it.
  It has never heard of altarr.
- **A loop over time steps.** Each step is one planned read, and steps
  that fall in chunks already read cost nothing, so the loop makes one
  fetch call per layer of chunks it enters.
- **After `dimnames<-` on a copy.** R does not copy the data; it wraps
  the object in its own ALTREP wrapper class. The patch makes the wrapper
  forward the method, so a renamed array is still planned.

```{r}
book_elt(res)
```

## Where this reaches

The same thing holds further up the stack, in packages that sit on lazy
arrays:

- [ndr](https://hypertidy.github.io/ndr/) (labelled n-dimensional arrays,
  in the manner of xarray) selects with `do.call("[", ...)`. On stock R
  it has to detect a lazy array and call `altarr_extract()`. With the
  method it does not need to know.
- [GDAL7](https://github.com/rgdal-dev/GDAL7) presents GDAL
  multidimensional arrays and raster bands with `as_altarr()`. Given the
  whole request, a band indexed as `b[rows, cols]` can be one GDAL read of
  the window, with one `AdviseRead` ahead of it.
- Any reader could do the same. The method is not specific to altarr:
  arrow, a NetCDF or HDF5 package, a database-backed matrix, a
  memory-mapped file class could each implement it.

## Still open

- **Wrapper classes in packages.** R's own wrapper forwards the method. A
  package that defines its own ALTREP view over another object (rray 0.2.0
  has one) cannot forward it, because the dispatch function is internal to
  R. Whether to export it is a question for R core. Not yet tested here.
- **Subassignment.** `x[i, j, k] <- value` on a lazy array materializes
  it. A write-side method would be the companion to this one; it is not
  part of this proposal.
- **`is.na()`** has no ALTREP hook, so `mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)` still
  walks elements. Subsetting first, then
  computing on the ordinary array that comes back, is the pattern that
  works, and it is the one this patch makes fast.
